Yes, I have. I went there with my family last winter.
Lucky you! What was it like when you saw the old tombs at Hegra?
It was breathtaking. The rocks were huge, and our guide told us lots of stories. Have you ever been there?
No, I haven't, but I'd really like to go. How many times have you performed Umrah?
I've performed it twice so far. The last time was in Ramadan, and it was very crowded but peaceful.
That sounds special. Have you ever tried a new sport, like climbing or surfing?
Yes! I tried out rock climbing last month. It was hard at first, but I loved it.

grammar.title: Present Perfect for Experiences vs Past Simple
grammar.ar: نستخدم المضارع التام (have/has + التصريف الثالث) للسؤال عن التجارب في الحياة دون تحديد وقت، مثل: Have you ever been to AlUla? وعندما نذكر وقتًا محددًا في الماضي (last year, in 2023) ننتقل إلى الماضي البسيط: I went there last year. انتبه: في العربية نقول «هل زرت؟» بصيغة الماضي، لكن في الإنجليزية نستخدم المضارع التام إذا لم نحدد الوقت.
examples: Have you ever eaten camel meat? Yes, I have. I tried it at a wedding last year.
I've never been on a plane, but I'd really like to fly to Japan one day.
How many times have you visited Madinah? I've visited it four times.

words.ex: My cousin's wedding was a memorable night for the whole family.
We were walking home when suddenly it started to rain heavily.
The crowd went crazy when Al-Hilal scored in the last minute.
Everyone stood up and cheered for the national team.
We have a big family gathering at my grandfather's house every Eid.
My mother burst into tears when she saw her brother after five years.

dialogue.t: Tell me about a day you'll never forget.
Sure! It was the first day of Eid last year. We were all sitting in my grandfather's majlis, drinking Arabic coffee.
Sounds nice. So what happened?
Well, while we were eating dates and chatting, someone knocked on the door. Just as my dad opened it, my uncle walked in!
Your uncle? Was it a surprise?
Yes! He lives in Canada, and nobody knew he was coming. My grandmother burst into tears.
Wow, that's so emotional! How did the day end?
At first, everyone was shocked, then we all hugged him, and in the end, we stayed up until midnight telling stories.

grammar.title: Past Continuous and Past Simple in Stories
grammar.ar: نستخدم الماضي المستمر (was/were + فعل ينتهي بـ ing) لوصف الخلفية أو حدث كان مستمرًا في الماضي، ونستخدم الماضي البسيط للحدث القصير الذي قطعه. نستخدم while غالبًا مع الحدث الطويل، و when أو just as مع الحدث المفاجئ. Just as تعني «في اللحظة نفسها التي…».
examples: I was watching the match when suddenly the electricity went off.
While we were driving to the stadium, my brother lost his ticket.
Just as the referee blew the whistle, Salem scored the winning goal.

words.ex: Checking my phone before bed is a bad habit I want to stop.
I used to be a picky eater, but now I eat almost everything.

words.ar: يتخلّص من عادة مع التقدّم في العمر
words.ex: My little brother is scared of the dark, but he'll grow out of it.
I took up swimming last year, and now I go three times a week.
Since I joined the debate club, I've become more confident.
These days I prefer reading online comics to watching cartoons.

dialogue.t: What were you like when you were a child?
I was very shy. I used to hide behind my mum when guests came to our house.
Really? You don't seem shy now!
No, I'm not. Since I started playing in a football team, I've become more confident.
That's great. What about food? Were you a picky eater?
Yes! I didn't use to eat vegetables at all, but these days I love salad, especially fattoush.
Ha! And what did you do in your free time?
When I was younger, I would watch cartoons every afternoon. Now I'd rather go cycling with my friends.

grammar.title: Used to and Would for Past Habits
grammar.ar: نستخدم used to + المصدر للتعبير عن عادات أو حالات في الماضي لم تعد موجودة الآن، وفي النفي والسؤال نحذف حرف d فنقول didn't use to و Did you use to. نستخدم would للأفعال المتكررة فقط في الماضي، ولا نستخدمها مع الحالات مثل be أو like أو have. للتعبير عن تغيّر مستمر حتى الآن نستخدم Since + الماضي البسيط مع المضارع التام.
examples: I used to be afraid of cats, but now I have two at home.
When I was seven, I would visit my grandparents in Abha every summer.
Did you use to play video games a lot? No, I didn't use to like them.

words.ex: We boarded the plane just ten minutes before it took off.
There was a two-hour delay because of a sandstorm.
Our luggage didn't arrive, so we had to buy new clothes.
We got a flat tyre on the road between Riyadh and Taif.
It turned out that the hotel was much closer than we thought.
A kind man at the airport helped us sort out the problem.

dialogue.t: Have you been on any family trips recently?
Yes, we drove from Riyadh to Abha in the summer holidays.
That's a long drive! Did anything go wrong?
Yes. Unfortunately, we got a flat tyre in the middle of nowhere, so we had to stop for two hours.
Oh no! Didn't you have a spare tyre?
We did, but it turned out that it was flat too! Luckily, a farmer stopped and took my dad to the nearest garage.
What a relief! When did you finally arrive?
Very late. The hotel restaurant had already closed by the time we got there. But the best part of the trip was the cool weather and the green mountains.

grammar.title: Past Perfect: The Earlier Past
grammar.ar: نستخدم الماضي التام (had + التصريف الثالث) لنوضّح أن حدثًا وقع قبل حدث آخر في الماضي. غالبًا نستخدمه مع by the time أو when أو already. الحدث الأقدم يكون بالماضي التام، والحدث الأحدث بالماضي البسيط، فيفهم المستمع ترتيب الأحداث بوضوح.
examples: The plane had already left by the time we reached the gate.
When we got to the beach, my sister realised she had forgotten her phone at home.
We had never seen snow before, so the trip to Turkey was really exciting.

words.ex: I always feel nervous before maths exams.
It was so embarrassing when I called my teacher Mum by mistake.
I was so relieved when I saw my exam results.
The week before the competition was really stressful.
My parents were proud of me when I won the Quran recitation competition.
I felt overwhelmed on my first day at the new school.

dialogue.t: Last week I had to give a speech in front of three hundred people. I was terrified!
That must have been really stressful! Did everything go well?
Not exactly. I dropped all my notes on the floor at the start.
Oh no! No wonder you felt nervous. Something similar happened to me in the school science competition.
Really? What happened?
My volcano model didn't work in front of the judges. It was really embarrassing because everyone was watching.
I can imagine! So, what was the result?
I couldn't believe that we still came second! I felt so proud and relieved when they announced our names.

grammar.title: -ed and -ing Adjectives and Must Have Been
grammar.ar: الصفات المنتهية بـ ed- تصف شعور الشخص (I was bored = كنت أشعر بالملل)، أما المنتهية بـ ing- فتصف الشيء أو الموقف الذي يسبّب الشعور (The film was boring = الفيلم مُملّ). وعندما نتفاعل مع قصة شخص آخر ونستنتج شعوره نستخدم That must have been + صفة، أي «لا بدّ أنه كان…». ونقول No wonder you felt… أي «لا عجب أنك شعرت بـ…».
examples: I was really excited because the match was so exciting.
You waited three hours at the airport? That must have been exhausting!
You didn't sleep before the exam? No wonder you felt tired.

words.ex: We got lost in the old souq in Jeddah because all the streets looked the same.
I started to panic when I couldn't find my passport.
Luckily, a shopkeeper let me use his phone to call my dad.
When our car broke down, my uncle came to the rescue.
Looking back, it was actually a funny day.
I realised that I should always keep my phone charged.

dialogue.t: OK, you have two minutes. Tell me your story.
One day, my family and I went to Al-Balad in Jeddah. I wanted to buy a gift for my friend, so I walked into a small shop alone.
Uh-oh. I think I know what's coming!
Yes! Unfortunately, when I came out, my family had disappeared. I got lost and started to panic because my phone battery was dead.
That must have been scary! What did you do?
Luckily, an old shopkeeper came to the rescue. He let me call my dad, and in the end, my family found me twenty minutes later.
Great story! How do you feel about it now?
Looking back, I realise that I should never walk off without telling my parents, and I always charge my phone now!

grammar.title: Story Structure and Narrative Linkers
grammar.ar: القصة الجيدة لها ثلاثة أجزاء: بداية (One day…) ومشكلة (Unfortunately…) ونهاية (Luckily… / In the end…). نستخدم أدوات الربط هذه لنساعد المستمع على متابعة الأحداث، ونرويها غالبًا بالماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر. ونختم القصة بعبارة Looking back, I realise that… لنذكر الدرس الذي تعلّمناه، ونستخدم بعدها المضارع لأننا نتحدث عن رأينا الآن.
examples: One day, I was playing football in the park when I hurt my ankle.
Unfortunately, the last bus had already left, but luckily my cousin drove past and gave me a lift.
In the end, we won the match, and looking back, I realise that teamwork is everything.

words.ex: In my opinion, art is the most relaxing subject at school.
I prefer action films to comedies because they are more exciting.
This new app is really entertaining, so I use it every evening.
Maths is challenging, but I feel proud when I solve a hard problem.
English is useful because I can understand games and films without subtitles.
Some people think history is boring, but I find it interesting.

dialogue.t: In my opinion, science is the most interesting subject because we do experiments in the lab.
That's interesting! Do you like it more than maths?
Yes, I think science is better than maths since it explains how the world works. What's your view on video games, teacher?
As far as I'm concerned, some games are great for problem-solving, but players shouldn't spend all day on them.
I agree. I think strategy games are better than shooting games since you have to plan and think carefully.
Good point. And which app do you use the most?
In my opinion, Duolingo is the best app because it makes learning languages fun and quick.

grammar.title: Giving reasons with 'because' and 'since'
grammar.ar: نستخدم because و since لنشرح سبب رأينا، ومعناهما «لأنّ». بعد كل منهما نضع جملة كاملة فيها فاعل وفعل، مثل: because it is fun. لا نقول because fun بدون فعل. يمكن أن تأتي since في بداية الجملة أيضًا، وهي أكثر رسمية قليلًا من because.
examples: I love English because I can talk to people from other countries.
I think football games are better than racing games since you can play with friends online.
Since this film has amazing special effects, I think everyone should watch it.

words.ex: Our class had a debate about whether homework is necessary.
I disagree with my friend, but we are still good friends.
You made a good point about students needing more sleep.
Her argument was strong because she gave real examples.
It's important to respect other people's opinions, even when you disagree.
Having too many tests in one week can be very stressful.

dialogue.t: I think students should have homework every day. It helps us remember what we learned.
I see what you mean, but daily homework can be really stressful for some students.
That's a good point; however, if the homework is short, it won't take much time.
I'm not sure I agree, because students also need time for sports, family and rest.
OK, I partly agree, but without practice, many students forget the lesson quickly.
True. Maybe teachers could give homework three times a week instead.
That sounds fair. I think we can agree to disagree on the rest!

grammar.title: Contrasting ideas with 'but' and 'however'
grammar.ar: نستخدم but و however لنُظهر فكرة مختلفة أو معاكسة، ومعناهما «لكنّ». تأتي but في وسط الجملة لتربط جزأين معًا. أما however فهي أكثر رسمية، وتأتي غالبًا في بداية جملة جديدة بعد نقطة أو فاصلة منقوطة (;) ويتبعها فاصلة. استخدامهما يجعل اعتراضك مهذّبًا ومنظّمًا.
examples: I see what you mean, but homework at weekends is too much.
That's a good point; however, students need time to relax.
Homework helps us practise. However, it shouldn't take more than an hour.

words.ex: One advantage of smartphones is that you can contact your family quickly.
A big disadvantage of online gaming is that it can waste a lot of time.
My parents limit my screen time to two hours on school days.
Some teenagers become addicted to social media and check it all the time.
I use messaging apps to keep in touch with my cousins in Riyadh.
Looking at a screen late at night can be harmful to your sleep.

dialogue.t: One advantage of social media is that you can keep in touch with friends and family easily.
That's true. On the other hand, some teenagers spend hours scrolling and don't sleep enough.
I think it depends on how you use it. If you set a time limit, it's not harmful.
Maybe. The problem with online gaming is that it's very easy to become addicted.
Yes, but one advantage of gaming is that you learn teamwork and quick thinking.
I agree with that. What about smartphones at school?
The problem with phones at school is that students get distracted by notifications.

grammar.title: Using -ing after prepositions
grammar.ar: عندما يأتي فعل بعد حرف جر مثل of أو with أو about، نضيف إليه ing-. لذلك نقول: One advantage of using، وليس of use أو of to use. هذه قاعدة مهمة لأن العربية لا تملك شكلًا مشابهًا، فيخطئ فيها كثير من المتعلمين.
examples: One advantage of playing online is that you can meet players from around the world.
The problem with checking your phone at night is that you can't sleep well.
I'm worried about spending too much time on social media.

words.ex: Our school has a rule that students must wear a uniform.
Students should be allowed to use tablets for research in class.
Some schools ban phones completely during the school day.
It isn't fair to punish the whole class for one student's mistake.
A good alternative to a phone ban is a phone box in each classroom.
Noise from the corridor is a big distraction during exams.

dialogue.t: I think students should be allowed to bring phones to class.
Really? I don't think phones should be allowed in lessons. They're a big distraction.
But if students used phones for research, they would learn faster.
Maybe, but if students had phones on their desks, they would play games instead of studying.
OK, that's a fair point. A better idea would be to use phones only when the teacher says so.
I like that. And what about breaks? I think they're too short.
Me too. If students had longer breaks, they would concentrate better in the afternoon.
Exactly. A better idea would be to add ten minutes to lunch break.

grammar.title: The second conditional: imagining results
grammar.ar: نستخدم الجملة الشرطية الثانية لنتخيل موقفًا غير حقيقي الآن ونتيجته. التركيب هو: If + فعل ماضٍ، ثم would + الفعل في صورته الأساسية. رغم أن الفعل بعد if في الماضي، فإن المعنى عن الحاضر أو المستقبل. لا نضع would بعد if مباشرة، فنقول: If students had، وليس If students would have.
examples: If students had longer breaks, they would feel less tired.
If the school banned phones, students would talk to each other more.
If I were the head teacher, I would allow students to choose their own projects.

words.ex: I admire players who work hard and never give up.
He is so talented that he can score with both feet.
Our favourite team won the championship last season.
The team has amazing team spirit, so they always help each other.
Many fans think Salem Al-Dawsari is a legend of Saudi football.
A good athlete should be a role model for young people.

dialogue.t: The reason why I admire Salem Al-Dawsari is that he always plays his best in big matches.
He's a great player, but why do you think he's the best?
He's not only fast but also very clever with the ball.
Some people prefer foreign stars in the Saudi Pro League. What do you think?
Of course they're talented, but I think Al-Dawsari is much more important to Saudi fans than any other player.
Hmm, you might be right. Remember his goal against Argentina at the 2022 World Cup?
Yes! Anyone who has seen that goal would agree that he's a real hero.
OK, you've almost persuaded me. He's definitely a great role model.

grammar.title: Adding emphasis with 'not only ... but also'
grammar.ar: نستخدم not only ... but also لنضيف معلومتين إيجابيتين ونؤكد الثانية، ومعناها «ليس فقط ... بل أيضًا». يجب أن يكون ما بعد not only وما بعد but also من النوع نفسه: صفتان، أو اسمان، أو فعلان. هذا التركيب يجعل كلامك أكثر إقناعًا في النقاش.
examples: Al-Hilal is not only successful but also popular across Asia.
She is not only a fast runner but also a great team captain.
Playing sports not only keeps you fit but also helps you make friends.

words.ex: In my free time, I usually play football with my brothers.
Personally, I'd rather read a book than watch TV.
After a long school day, I like to relax by drawing.
In the exam, try to develop your answer with a reason and an example.
Technology has changed the way we study at home.
To sum up, I think hobbies are good for both body and mind.

dialogue.t: What do you usually do in your free time?
Personally, I'd say my favourite thing is swimming. For example, I go to the pool with my cousins every Friday.
Why do you enjoy it so much?
It helps me relax after school. Another thing is that it keeps me fit and healthy.
Do you think technology helps students at school?
Yes, I think so. For example, we use online quizzes to revise before tests. Another thing is that we can watch videos to understand difficult topics.
Are there any problems with it?
Sometimes students get distracted. So, to sum up, technology is helpful if we use it in the right way.

grammar.title: Organising a longer answer with linking phrases
grammar.ar: في اختبارات المحادثة، لا يكفي أن تجيب بكلمة أو جملة واحدة. نظّم إجابتك هكذا: ابدأ برأيك (Personally, I'd say...)، ثم أعطِ مثالًا (For example...)، ثم أضف فكرة أخرى (Another thing is that...)، وأخيرًا لخّص (So, to sum up...). هذه العبارات تجعل إجابتك واضحة ومترابطة وتساعدك على الحصول على درجة أعلى.
examples: Personally, I'd say weekends are the best time to try new hobbies.
For example, last month I started learning to cook simple dishes.
Another thing is that school clubs help students discover their talents, so, to sum up, free time activities are very important.

words.ex: My dad has already booked tickets for Boulevard World on Friday.
I'm thinking of joining a football summer camp in July.
We're visiting our relatives in Jeddah during the holidays.
I might stay up late on Thursday because there's no school the next day.
Our trip depends on whether my dad can take time off work.
I'm definitely going to the concert. I have my ticket already!

dialogue.t: What are you doing this weekend?
I'm going to Boulevard World with my cousins on Friday evening. My dad has already booked the tickets.
Lucky you! What about the summer holidays?
Nothing is fixed yet. I'm thinking of joining a football summer camp.
That sounds fun. Are you going to travel?
We might visit my grandparents in Abha if my dad gets time off work.
I'm going to stay in Riyadh, but I might go to a Riyadh Season concert if I can get tickets.
Let me know. Maybe we can go together!

grammar.title: Future plans: present continuous, going to, might
grammar.ar: نستخدم المضارع المستمر (I'm meeting...) للخطط الثابتة المرتّبة مسبقاً مع وقت أو مكان محدد، ونستخدم going to للنية أو القرار الذي اتخذناه من قبل. أما might فتعبّر عن احتمال غير مؤكد، وكثيراً ما تأتي مع if لذكر الشرط. وتُستخدم I'm thinking of + فعل ينتهي بـ ing لفكرة ما زلنا نفكر فيها. لاحظ أن العربية تستخدم «سـ» أو «سوف» في كل هذه الحالات، لكن الإنجليزية تفرّق بينها حسب درجة التأكد.
examples: I'm playing football with my friends on Saturday afternoon.
We might go camping in the desert if the weather is nice.
I'm thinking of learning to swim this summer.

words.ex: Why don't we go to the new theme park next weekend?
Let's meet up at the mall entrance at five.
Would Saturday evening suit you?
My brother can pick us up from school.
The park is always crowded at weekends, so let's go early.
It's too hot in the morning. How about going in the evening instead?

dialogue.t: Why don't we go to the theme park next weekend?
Great idea! How about going on Saturday morning?
That sounds good, but what if it's too hot? It's still summer.
True. How about going in the evening instead? It opens at four.
Perfect. Would five o'clock suit you?
Yes, five is fine. How are we going to get there?
My brother can pick us up and drive us. We can meet at the mall entrance near your house.
Let's meet there at quarter to five then. See you on Saturday!

grammar.title: Making and responding to suggestions
grammar.ar: نستخدم Why don't we + فعل مجرد، و How about + فعل ينتهي بـ ing لاقتراح شيء. بعد How about نستخدم صيغة ing وليس to، فلا نقول How about to go. لإبداء قلق أو مشكلة نقول That sounds good, but what if...، وللاتفاق النهائي نقول Let's ... then. أما Would ... suit you? فهي طريقة مهذبة لنسأل إن كان الوقت أو المكان مناسباً.
examples: Why don't we take the metro? It's faster.
How about meeting at the café before the film?
Would Thursday afternoon suit you?

words.ex: I'm really stressed out about my science exam.
It might help to revise a little every day.
You'd better take a break. You've been studying for three hours.
Have you tried breathing slowly to calm down?
I always argue with my sister about the TV remote.
If I were you, I'd reduce my screen time before bed.

dialogue.t: You look tired. Are you OK?
Not really. I'm so stressed about my maths exam, and I can't sleep at night.
Have you tried putting your phone away an hour before bed?
No, I usually watch videos until midnight.
If I were you, I'd stop that. It might help to read a book instead.
Maybe. Also, I keep arguing with my brother because he's noisy when I'm revising.
You'd better talk to him calmly and explain. Whatever you do, don't shout at him. It'll only make things worse.
Thanks, that's really useful advice.

grammar.title: Giving advice
grammar.ar: عبارة If I were you, I'd + فعل مجرد تعني «لو كنت مكانك لـ...»، ونستخدم were مع I في هذه العبارة. أما You'd better (اختصار You had better) + فعل مجرد فهي نصيحة قوية فيها تحذير، ولا نضع to بعدها. العبارتان Have you tried + ing? و It might help to + فعل مجرد نصيحتان ألطف وأقل إلزاماً. ونستخدم Whatever you do, don't... للتحذير من أمر مهم جداً.
examples: If I were you, I'd make a study timetable.
You'd better go to bed early tonight.
Whatever you do, don't leave all your revision until the last day.

words.ex: An honest person would return the money.
I'd hand the wallet in to the police station.
I'd try to find the owner of the phone.
What would you do if you won a big prize?
If I had a lot of money, I would donate some to charity.
I wouldn't open the bag unless I needed to find a name.

dialogue.t: What would you do if you found a wallet with a lot of money in it?
I'd probably hand it in to the police unless there was an ID card inside. Then I'd try to contact the owner myself.
Really? Wouldn't you keep any of the money?
No, I wouldn't keep it because it isn't mine. It wouldn't be honest.
Good point. What would you do if you won a million riyals?
If I had that much money, I would buy a new house for my parents. What about you?
I'd donate some to charity, and I'd travel around the world with my family.
That sounds amazing!

grammar.title: The second conditional
grammar.ar: نستخدم الشرط الثاني للحديث عن مواقف خيالية أو غير محتملة في الحاضر أو المستقبل. التركيب هو: If + الماضي البسيط، ثم would + فعل مجرد. ورغم أن الفعل بعد if في الماضي، فإن المعنى عن الحاضر أو المستقبل وليس عن الماضي. وكلمة unless تعني «إلا إذا» وتساوي if ... not.
examples: If I had more free time, I would learn to play the oud.
What would you do if you met your favourite footballer?
I wouldn't lend him my phone because he always breaks things.

words.ex: It's likely that more people will use public transport in the future.
By 2030, many buildings will have switched to renewable energy.
I hope that there will be less air pollution in our cities.
NEOM is planned to be a sustainable city.
It's likely that electric cars will become more popular.
I doubt that people will stop driving completely.

dialogue.t: What do you think Riyadh will be like in 2030?
In the future, there will probably be fewer cars on the roads. By 2030, the Riyadh Metro will have changed how people travel.
I agree. It's likely that more people will use public transport.
What about NEOM? Do you think people will be living in The Line by then?
I hope that some people will, but I doubt that it will be finished by 2030. It's a huge project.
True. I hope that our cities will be greener too, with more trees and parks.
Me too. It's likely that we'll use more solar energy because we have so much sunshine.
Exactly! The future looks exciting.

grammar.title: Making predictions: will, will have + past participle
grammar.ar: نستخدم will للتنبؤ بالمستقبل، ونضيف probably أو It's likely that لتوضيح درجة التأكد. ونستخدم المستقبل التام (will have + التصريف الثالث للفعل) لحدث سيكتمل قبل وقت محدد في المستقبل، مثل By 2030. بعد I hope that و I doubt that نضع جملة كاملة غالباً مع will. لاحظ مكان probably: بعد will في الجملة المثبتة (will probably) وقبل won't في المنفية (probably won't).
examples: In the future, there will probably be more electric buses.
By 2030, the city will have planted millions of new trees.
I doubt that flying cars will be common by then.

words.ex: Our school is organising a charity event next month.
We want to raise money for children in need.
Which option do you think is best?
A bake sale would be easy to organise.
We have a small budget, so we can't spend too much.
We need to make a decision by Thursday.

dialogue.t: We need to choose an idea for our school charity event. Which option do you think is best?
I think a bake sale would be useful because everyone loves sweets and it's cheap to organise.
That's true. But what about a sports day? It would be more fun for the students.
It would be fun, but we'd need a big budget and a lot of time to plan it.
Good point. A book swap is another option. It would encourage reading.
Yes, but it wouldn't raise much money. I think we should choose the bake sale because it's easy and we can raise money quickly.
OK. Shall we decide on the bake sale, then?
Yes, let's do it! I can make a list of who will bring what.

grammar.title: Discussing options and reaching a decision
grammar.ar: نستخدم would + فعل مجرد للحديث عن النتائج المتوقعة لخيار لم نختره بعد، مثل It would be fun. ونبرّر رأينا دائماً باستخدام because. أما Shall we decide on...? فهي سؤال لاقتراح القرار النهائي، و I think we should choose... لإبداء رأينا في الخيار الأفضل مع ذكر السبب.
examples: A car wash would be useful because lots of parents drive to school.
Shall we decide on the book swap?
I think we should choose the bake sale because it doesn't cost much.

words.ex: In the background, there are some tall buildings and a mosque.
In the foreground, a man is holding a basket of dates.
The market looks very crowded, so it might be the weekend.
There's a small stall selling spices and fresh fruit.
The fans are cheering because their team has just scored.
The students seem to be working on a group project.

dialogue.t: OK, your turn. What can you see in this photo?
In this picture I can see a busy market. There are lots of people walking between the stalls.
What do you think the woman in the foreground is doing?
It looks like she's buying vegetables. She might be choosing tomatoes because she's holding one up and looking at it carefully.
And what about the people at the back?
In the background, there's a man with a big cart. I'm not sure, but maybe he's bringing more boxes to the stalls.
Why do you think it's so crowded?
They might be shopping for a special occasion, like Eid, because everyone seems to be carrying lots of bags.

grammar.title: Guessing with might / may / could + be + -ing
grammar.ar: عندما لا نكون متأكدين مما يحدث في الصورة، نستخدم might أو may أو could ثم be ثم الفعل مع ing. لا نضيف to بعد هذه الأفعال، فلا نقول might to be. ونستخدم It looks like أو I'm not sure, but maybe للتخمين أيضًا. وتذكّر أن الإنجليزية تحتاج دائمًا إلى فعل be في المضارع المستمر، فنقول He is playing وليس He playing.
examples: They might be waiting for the bus because they keep looking at the road.
The boy could be feeling nervous before his exam.
It looks like the fans are celebrating a goal.

words.ex: Online learning is convenient because you can study at home.
My online course is flexible, so I can choose when to study.
Living in a small town is usually more affordable than living in a big city.
One big advantage of classroom learning is that you can ask the teacher questions face to face.
Riyadh is very hot in summer, whereas Abha is much cooler.
I prefer studying with my friends because it's more fun.

dialogue.t: Which do you think is better, online learning or classroom learning?
Well, both online and classroom learning have advantages. Online learning is far more flexible than going to school every day.
That's true. But is it as useful?
Not really. For me, online lessons are not as interesting as real classes. It's hard to concentrate at home.
I agree. Whereas online classes can be lonely, in the classroom you can work with your friends.
Exactly. And the teacher can help you straight away.
So which one would you choose?
Overall, I'd prefer classroom learning because I learn better when I can talk to people face to face.

grammar.title: Comparing: not as ... as / far more ... than
grammar.ar: نستخدم not as + الصفة + as لنقول إن شيئًا أقل من شيء آخر في صفة معينة. ونستخدم far أو much قبل صيغة المقارنة للتأكيد على أن الفرق كبير، مثل far more expensive أو much cheaper. لا نجمع more مع الصفة التي تنتهي بـ er، فلا نقول more cheaper أو more better. وبعد than نذكر الشيء الثاني مباشرة دون تكرار الفعل غالبًا.
examples: Jeddah is not as hot as Riyadh in the summer.
Learning in class is far more interesting than watching videos alone.
The bus is much cheaper than a taxi, but it's slower.

words.ex: The main ingredients of kabsa are rice, chicken and spices.
First, the coffee beans are roasted until they turn light brown.
After that, the beans are ground with some cardamom.
Boil the water for about ten minutes.
The coffee is poured into small cups called finjan.
Arabic coffee is usually served with dates.

dialogue.t: I've always wanted to know how Arabic coffee is made. Can you explain it?
Sure! First, the coffee beans are roasted in a pan. My grandfather likes them light, not dark.
Then what happens?
After that, the beans are ground and added to boiling water. Then it's left to boil for a few minutes.
What about the cardamom? I love that smell.
Once the coffee is ready, the cardamom is added to the dallah. Some people add saffron too.
And how do you drink it?
It is usually served with dates. Once your cup is empty, you shake it gently if you don't want any more.

grammar.title: Present Simple Passive for processes
grammar.ar: عند شرح طريقة صنع شيء ما، نهتم بالعملية أكثر من الشخص الذي يقوم بها، لذلك نستخدم المبني للمجهول. صيغته: is أو are + التصريف الثالث للفعل (past participle). نستخدم is مع المفرد وare مع الجمع، ولا يجوز حذف is أو are كما يحدث أحيانًا عند التفكير بالعربية. انتبه إلى الأفعال الشاذة مثل grind تصبح ground.
examples: First, the rice is washed and left in water for twenty minutes.
After that, the spices are added to the chicken.
Kabsa is usually served on a large plate and shared with the family.

words.ex: I really admire my aunt because she never gives up.
My older brother is a great role model for me.
My science teacher inspired me to become an engineer.
She is very patient and always explains things again if we don't understand.
My grandfather is so generous that he helps everyone in the neighbourhood.
My mother has had a big influence on the way I think.

dialogue.t: Now, I'd like you to talk about a person you admire. You have one to two minutes.
OK. I'd like to talk about my grandmother. She lives in Taif, and I visit her every summer.
What kind of person is she?
She is someone who always thinks about other people first. She's very generous and patient.
Can you give an example?
Yes. When I was younger, she taught me to read. What I admire most is that she never got angry, even when I made lots of mistakes.
How has she influenced you?
She has taught me to be kind and to work hard. She's my role model, and I hope I can be like her one day.

grammar.title: Describing people with who (relative clauses)
grammar.ar: نستخدم who لنضيف معلومات عن شخص، مثل: someone who / a teacher who. بعد who يأتي الفعل مباشرة، ولا نكرر الضمير كما نفعل في العربية، فلا نقول She is someone who she helps people، بل She is someone who helps people. وتذكر إضافة s للفعل في المضارع مع المفرد مثل helps وlistens.
examples: He is someone who always listens to my problems.
I admire teachers who make lessons fun.
My uncle is a doctor who works in a hospital in Dammam.

words.ex: I chose AlUla as the topic of my presentation.
A good presentation has a clear structure: a beginning, a middle and an end.
In the introduction, I'll tell the audience what my talk is about.
In my conclusion, I'll repeat the main ideas.
Try to look at the audience when you speak.
Diriyah is an important heritage site near Riyadh.

dialogue.t: Have you decided on a topic for your presentation yet?
Yes, I'm going to talk about AlUla. It's an amazing heritage site, and I visited it last year.
Great choice! How are you going to start?
I'll say, "Today I'm going to talk about AlUla and why everyone should visit it." Then I'll show a photo.
And what are your main points?
Firstly, I'll talk about its history. Secondly, I'll explain what tourists can do there, like hiking and visiting Hegra.
Remember to include an example. The audience will love it.
Good idea. I'll say, "Let me give you an example: Elephant Rock looks exactly like an elephant!" To conclude, I'll ask them to plan a trip there.

grammar.title: Talking about plans: be going to
grammar.ar: نستخدم be going to + الفعل الأساسي للحديث عن خطط قررناها مسبقًا. يجب أن نستخدم am أو is أو are قبل going to، فلا نقول I going to talk. ونستخدم will عادةً عندما نقرر شيئًا في لحظة الكلام، أما going to فللخطة المحضّرة مسبقًا. يأتي بعد to الفعل في صيغته الأصلية بدون ing.
examples: Today I'm going to talk about my favourite hobby, photography.
We are going to show some pictures at the end.
Is she going to talk about her future career?

words.ex: Can I clarify one point from my presentation?
As I mentioned earlier, the museum opens at nine.
That's an interesting point. I hadn't thought about it.
Could you repeat the question, please? I didn't hear it.
She looked confident and spoke clearly.
I was nervous at the start, but I felt better after a minute.

dialogue.t: Thank you, that was a great presentation about becoming a pilot. I have a few questions.
Thank you. Of course, go ahead.
Why do you think it's a good job for young Saudis today?
That's a good question. I think there are more airlines and airports now, so we will need many new pilots.
You said the training is hard. In what way?
Sorry, could you repeat the question, please?
Sure. You said pilot training is difficult. Why is that?
Oh, what I meant was that you have to study a lot of science and maths. As I mentioned earlier, you also need many hours of flying practice.

grammar.title: Polite requests and clarifying: Could you ...? / What I meant was ...
grammar.ar: نستخدم Could you + الفعل الأساسي لنطلب شيئًا بأدب، وهو أكثر لباقة من Can you أو استخدام الأمر مباشرة مثل Repeat. وعندما نريد توضيح فكرة قلناها سابقًا نستخدم What I meant was + جملة كاملة، ويكون meant بصيغة الماضي لأننا نتحدث عن كلام قيل قبل قليل. ويمكن إضافة please في آخر الطلب لمزيد من الأدب.
examples: Could you repeat the question, please?
Could you speak a little more slowly, please?
What I meant was that the trip is expensive, not that it's boring.

units.cando: Can narrate a past experience or event in detail, describing feelings and reactions and linking events in a clear sequence.
lessons: Have You Ever...?
Swap real experiences with the teacher, such as trying a new sport, visiting AlUla or performing Umrah, and ask follow-up questions to keep the conversation going.
Have you ever ...? / Yes, I have. I ... last ... / No, I haven't, but I'd really like to ... / What was it like when you ...? / How many times have you ...?
A Day I'll Never Forget
Tell the story of a memorable day, such as a big football match, a family Eid gathering or a surprise, with clear background details and key events.
I was ...ing when suddenly ... / While we were ..., ... / At first ..., then ..., and in the end ... / Just as ..., ...
Then and Now
Compare your childhood habits, hobbies and opinions with your life today, and explain why things have changed.
I used to ..., but now I ... / I didn't use to ..., but these days I ... / When I was younger, I would ... / Since I started ..., I've become more ...
Travel Tales
Describe a family trip inside or outside Saudi Arabia, including a problem that happened on the way and how it was solved.
We had already ... by the time ... / It turned out that ... / The best part of the trip was ... / Unfortunately, ..., so we had to ...
Feelings and Reactions
Talk about how you felt during exciting, embarrassing or stressful moments, such as exams, competitions or meeting someone new, and react to the teacher's stories.
I felt so ... when ... / It was really ...ing because ... / I couldn't believe that ... / That must have been ...! / No wonder you felt ...
Story Time Challenge
Tell a two-minute story with a beginning, a problem and an ending using picture prompts or a real memory, then answer the teacher's follow-up questions.
One day, ... / Unfortunately, ... / Luckily, ... / In the end, ... / Looking back, I realise that ...

units.cando: Can give and justify opinions on familiar topics, agree or disagree politely, and respond to other people's viewpoints in a discussion.
lessons: What Do You Think?
Share and explain your opinions about school subjects, video games, films and apps, and ask for the teacher's opinion in return.
In my opinion, ... because ... / I think ... is better than ... since ... / What's your view on ...? / As far as I'm concerned, ...
Agree to Disagree
Discuss a debatable statement, such as 'Students should have homework every day', and practise disagreeing politely while showing respect.
I see what you mean, but ... / That's a good point; however, ... / I'm not sure I agree, because ... / I partly agree, but ...
Screens and Social Media
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of smartphones, social media and online gaming for teenagers.
One advantage of ... is that ... / On the other hand, ... / It depends on how ... / The problem with ... is that ...
School Rules Debate
Argue for or against a school rule, such as phones in class or longer breaks, and suggest a fair alternative.
Students should be allowed to ... / I don't think ... should ... / If students ..., they would ... / A better idea would be to ...
Sports and Heroes
Talk about athletes or teams you admire, such as players in the Saudi Pro League, and try to persuade the teacher that your choice is the best.
The reason why I admire ... is that ... / Not only ... but also ... / ... is much more ... than ... / Anyone who has seen ... would agree that ...
Mini Discussion Round
Take part in an exam-style general discussion about free time, school or technology, developing each answer with reasons and examples.
Personally, I'd say ... / For example, ... / Another thing is that ... / So, to sum up, ...

units.cando: Can discuss future plans and hypothetical situations, make and respond to suggestions, and give advice on everyday problems.
lessons: Weekend and Holiday Plans
Talk about your plans for the weekend, Riyadh Season or the summer holidays, explaining which plans are fixed and which are still possible.
I'm going to ... / I'm ...ing with ... on ... / I might ... if ... / I'm thinking of ...ing
Making Arrangements
Plan an outing with a friend, such as a trip to a theme park, and agree on the time, place and transport.
Why don't we ...? / How about ...ing? / That sounds good, but what if ...? / Let's ... then. / Would ... suit you?
Giving Advice
Help a friend who is stressed about exams, struggling to sleep or arguing with a sibling by giving practical advice.
If I were you, I'd ... / You'd better ... / Have you tried ...ing? / It might help to ... / Whatever you do, don't ...
What Would You Do?
Discuss imaginary situations, such as finding a lost wallet or winning a big prize, and explain your choices.
If I had ..., I would ... / I'd probably ... unless ... / What would you do if ...? / I wouldn't ... because ...
Our City, Our Future
Make predictions about life in Saudi cities by 2030, including projects like NEOM, transport and the environment.
In the future, there will probably be ... / By 2030, ... will have ... / I hope that ... / It's likely that ... / I doubt that ...
Solve It Together
Complete a collaborative task with the teacher by choosing the best idea for a school charity event and reaching a final decision.
Which option do you think is best? / ... would be useful because ... / Shall we decide on ...? / I think we should choose ... because ...

units.cando: Can give a short prepared presentation on a familiar topic, describe photos and processes, and answer follow-up questions with reasonable fluency.
lessons: Describing a Photo
Describe a photo of people at a market, a stadium or a classroom in detail, and guess what is happening and why.
In this picture I can see ... / It looks like ... / They might be ...ing because ... / In the background, ... / I'm not sure, but maybe ...
Comparing Choices
Compare two options, such as online and classroom learning or two different cities, and say which you prefer and why.
... is not as ... as ... / ... is far more ... than ... / Both ... and ... / Whereas ..., ... / Overall, I'd prefer ... because ...
How Is It Made?
Explain a process step by step, such as preparing Arabic coffee or kabsa, or how a mobile app is created.
First, ... is ... / After that, ... are added to ... / It is usually served with ... / Once it's ..., you ...
Talk About a Person
Answer an exam-style long turn about someone you admire, such as a family member, teacher or public figure, speaking for one to two minutes.
I'd like to talk about ... / He/She is someone who ... / What I admire most is ... / ... has taught me ...
Planning a Presentation
Plan a short presentation on a topic you care about, such as a hobby, a Saudi heritage site or a future career, with a clear structure.
Today I'm going to talk about ... / Firstly, ... Secondly, ... / Let me give you an example: ... / To conclude, ...
Presentation Day
Deliver a two- to three-minute presentation, then answer the teacher's questions and clarify any points when needed.
That's a good question. I think ... / Could you repeat the question, please? / What I meant was ... / As I mentioned earlier, ...
